rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for the flavor or taste of something.

example.english: The taste of this soup is very strong.
example.jyutping: nei1 wun2 tong1 ge3 mei6 dou6 hou2 nung4

rows.note: Use this everyday choice when asking someone to sample food or drink.

example.english: Taste this iced lemon tea first.
example.jyutping: nei5 si3 haa5 ni1 bui1 dung3 ling4 caa4 sin1

rows.note: Use this when describing how food or drink tastes when eaten or drunk.

example.english: This cake has a lovely sweet taste.
example.jyutping: nei1 go3 daan6 gou1 sik6 lok6 hou2 hoeng1 tim4

rows.note: Use this when saying that something has a particular flavor, such as a garlic taste.

example.english: This soup has a garlic taste.
example.jyutping: nei1 wun2 tong1 jau5 syun3 mei6

rows.note: Use this for a person's preferences, especially in food, entertainment, or similar choices.

example.english: Our taste is different; I like spicy food.
example.traditional: 我哋口味唔同，我鍾意食辣嘢。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 hau2 mei6 m4 tung4 ngo5 zung1 ji3 sik6 laat6 je5

rows.note: Use this for aesthetic taste or discernment, as in someone's taste in clothes or design.

example.english: They have very good taste in clothes.
example.jyutping: keoi5 gaan2 saam1 hou2 jau5 ban2 mei6

rows.note: Use this for experiencing an emotion or sensation rather than sampling food.

example.english: I got a firsthand taste of an earthquake's power.
example.traditional: 我親身感受過地震嘅威力。
example.jyutping: ngo5 can1 san1 gam2 sau6 gwo3 dei6 zan3 ge3 wai1 lik6

rows.note: Use this when “a taste of” means a limited or introductory experience of something.

example.english: This workshop lets you have a taste of new technology.
example.traditional: 呢個工作坊畀你體驗吓新科技。
example.jyutping: nei1 go3 gung1 zok3 fong1 bei2 nei5 tai2 jim6 haa5 san1 fo1 gei6
